author: Washington Irving
title: Rip Van Winkle
edition: London: William Heinemann; New York: Doubleday, Page & Co. Cheaper issue (1916), new impression 1919, as stated in the printed publication history reproduced by PG60976. Story text only; illustration captions excluded; prose hard wraps reflowed. The separate introduction, Note and Postscript are outside the selected main-narrative scenes. The library text holds Irving's whole Rip Van Winkle as this edition prints it, with its introduction, note and postscript; Rackham's illustrations and their captions are not held.

rights.basis: The original-English text in this 1919 edition was published well before 1931 and its US term has expired. The named Project Gutenberg catalogue explicitly records public domain in the USA.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg 60976 plain text (UTF-8) from the PG mirror aleph.pglaf.org. Kept Irving's text from the Cartwright motto through the INTRODUCTION, the tale, the NOTE and the POSTSCRIPT; removed the PG header and footer, the publisher's list of Rackham books, the title and publication-history pages, the list of illustrations, every illustration marker and caption, the printer's imprint and the transcriber's note. The book's title (RIP VAN WINKLE, from its title page) is a level-1 heading and the four section titles level-2 headings; prose lines joined with single spaces, the transcription's spacing within lines kept; the indented motto, with its right-set attribution, is a stanza with indentation removed.
